name: Question 1
problem:
The rate of growth of the bear population $P(t)$ in a certain forest follows the logistic growth model

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=0.2P(4\,500-P),
$$

where $t$ is the time, in years. Find an expression for the bear population after $t$ years, given that there were $150$ bears initially.
worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
\frac{dP}{dt}=kP(a-P),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>P$ is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{a}{1+C{e}^{-akt}}.
$$

In this case, the constant of proportionality is $k=0.2,$ and the carrying capacity is $a=4\,500.$ 

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-(4\,500\cdot 0.2)t}}=\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

We now substitute the initial condition $P(0)=150$ and solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4\,500}{1+C{e}^{-900\cdot 0}} & =150 \\ 1+C & =\frac{4\,500}{150} \\ C & =30-1 \\  & =29.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
P(t)=\frac{4\,500}{1+29{e}^{-900t}}.
$$

Question 1
?

The rate of growth of the bear population P(t) in a certain forest follows the logistic growth model

dPdt=0.2P(4500−P),

where t is the time, in years. Find an expression for the bear population after t years, given that there were 150 bears initially.

a
P(t)=45001−29e−900t
b
P(t)=45001+29e−900t
c
P(t)=45001+29e−90t
d
P(t)=45001+150e−900t
e
P(t)=30001−29e−900t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A logistic growth equation has the form

dPdt=kP(a−P),

where k>0 is a constant of proportionality, and a>P is the carrying capacity.

The general solution to the logistic growth equation is P(t)=a1+Ce−akt.

In this case, the constant of proportionality is k=0.2, and the carrying capacity is a=4500.

Therefore, the general solution to our equation is

P(t)=45001+Ce−(4500⋅0.2)t=45001+Ce−900t.

We now substitute the initial condition P(0)=150 and solve for C. We get

45001+Ce−900⋅0=1501+C=4500150C=30−1=29.

So, we have

P(t)=45001+29e−900t.
